summary: Built the pure §4 rubbing ledger. Content (packages/content/src/objectives): the four types in a fixed order, stable ids <type>-<copy> (slice 2 types x 4 = 8, alpha 4 x 3 = 12), objectiveRules in 20 Hz ticks (collect/claim 120, choice 100, repeat-win 3600, seat 1200, gold 50, PvP 20% capped at 50), pvpGoldTransfer, and zod schemas/validators for source sites and the source assignment. Simulation (packages/simulation/src/objectives): LedgerState, where each rubbing has exactly one location (source/player/cache/duel reservation) plus a revision; seeded assignSources/createLedger; the operations addPlayer, unlockSource, startCollect, startCacheClaim, progressChannel, cancelChannel, reserveDuel, reportDuelResult, chooseTheft, advanceLedger (default theft at the deadline), disconnectPlayer, reconnectPlayer, expireReservation and quitPlayer. Each is (state, request) -> {state, result}; a rejected request returns the identical state object. checkLedger/assertLedger check the invariant. Added one ./objectives subpath export to each package.json, and docs/objectives.md. Tests: 28 scenario tests and 10 content tests, plus a property test (3 seeds x 2 presets, about 2700-5100 operations per sequence). Every operation runs on a deep-frozen state and is followed by an invariant check. Each seed is replayed to the same hashState, and coverage assertions prove each rule actually happened. A manual mutation check (4 injected bugs) made the tests fail each time. Checks executed in the worktree after npm ci: npm run typecheck (exit 0), npm run test:unit (317/317; an earlier run had 1 timeout in the existing maps.test.ts at host load 12.5, after which I shrank my property test from ~11 s to ~4 s and the rerun passed), npm run test:integration (22/22), npm run build (exit 0, smoke passed). Also checked by hand that both new subpaths resolve to and load from dist/, and that tests/unit/purity.test.ts flags a Math.random planted in each new directory (planted files removed). Nothing committed.
open_assumptions: The slice preset uses the first two types in the fixed order: Sun and Moon.
'Fewest free sources' in the default theft counts sources whose rubbing is still sealed (locked or not). Rubbings in caches are not counted.
The repeated-win gold window is measured from the previous result tick of the same ordered winner/loser pair, whether or not that win paid gold.

A winner who leaves (quit or expiry) during the choice window takes no rubbing and no gold, and the duel settles at once. A loser who leaves during the window still loses the chosen or default rubbing, and the rest goes into a cache at the loser's exit position when the duel settles.

Leaving during a fight is a forfeit: the opponent wins, then normal theft and gold apply. 'Both forfeit on the same tick' is the caller reporting outcome 'cancelled', which moves nothing, like a draw.

The choice window opens whenever at least one type is eligible (even exactly one). A choice is accepted while tick < result tick + 100, and advanceLedger commits the default at tick >= deadline. The room must call advanceLedger once per tick before other requests.
Both duel players' rubbings stay reserved until the settlement commits, so neither player can collect, claim or be challenged during the choice window.
An interruption means a tick with no progress (progress must arrive at lastTick+1). A gap restarts the count from 0 at that tick. The caller is responsible for cancelling on movement or damage.
Player gold lives in the ledger (starting purse from the rules, or given at join). Other gold sources and sinks are left to a later economy feature.
Sources start locked, and unlockSource is the hook the ruin feature will call. The ledger does not require the slice's two sources per island to have different types.
The new subpaths still need to be added to scripts/smoke-build.ts at merge, as decisions.md says.
untested: scripts/smoke-build.ts does not load the two new subpaths (not in owned paths). Loading from dist/ was checked by hand only.
Nothing is wired into MatchRoom, so the per-tick advanceLedger cadence and the caller's position choices (nearest shoreline or respawn dock for caches) are not exercised end to end.
The property test calls advanceLedger only when a choice window is due (or at random, 10%), not on every tick. Scenario tests cover the exact deadline boundaries.
Performance with very many duels per match: activeDuelOf and findDuel are linear scans over all duels, settled ones included.

The existing packages/content/src/maps.test.ts can hit vitest's 5 s default timeout when the host is heavily loaded. It failed once at load 12.5 and passed on rerun. This is pre-existing and not caused by ledger logic, but parallel CPU load from other tests makes it more likely.
verify_yourself: That a winner who quits or expires during the 5-second theft choice window should take neither rubbing nor gold, which is my reading of §4's 'validate winner eligibility again at commit time'. §4 and §12 do not state this case explicitly.
